chapter: Small group, new sound and Europe
title: How the small group went over
summary: It lasted about two years, played small clubs and Canada, and the public did not take to it much.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Leading a band: running, choosing and keeping players

blocks.x: So the small group -- it only lasted about a couple of years? I mean, one way or another?
Yeah.
Did it go abroad?
No, no.
No. Didn't go abroad until '54.
We went about as far as Canada, and that's about it.
Oh. How did that go down with people?
It went alright, but I don't think they -- you know.
I mean --
I don't think they -- we had fun. We used to small places. We didn't play any big places. It was -- like -- small clubs and what-not, you know.
Yeah.
And, I don't think the general public really --
It was a little on the slick side I think.
They didn't -- I don't think they took to it too well.
I mean, the character of Basie music must have changed because -- I mean -- those guys -- that wasn't Basie music -- those guys, was it?
Mm hmm.
Clark and Charlie Rouse, and those guys?
No, well, it had a different feeling, but the only thing that kept it basic, basically was the rhythm section and Basie.
And, Basie. Yeah.
Yeah.
Well, Basie must have been a bit -- let's see -- I mean, he must have been wondering what direction to go and what to do.
But, they wind up -- you know what I mean -- it lasted -- I don't know if it lasted two years or not. Did it? Do you have that running for two years?
What?
Didn't it last about two years?
I think yes -- at the most.
Yeah. I know it's not over two years.
